title: China-to-Azerbaijan PPE Respirator (FFP Mask / KN95) Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Conformity Assessment — Azerbaijan National Certification for Respiratory PPE
rows.target_requirement: Azerbaijan requires national conformity certification for regulated goods including industrial PPE (respiratory protection). The certification system is administered by AZSTAND (Azerbaijan Standardisation Institute) and accredited national certification bodies. The conformity assessment process typically involves: (1) product type-testing against the applicable AZS or GOST-adopted standard (e.g. GOST 12.4.191 or AZS equivalent of EN 149) by a nationally accredited laboratory; (2) factory/production audit (depending on certification scheme); (3) issuance of a national conformity certificate (sertifikat sootvetstviya) valid for the Azerbaijan market. Neither EAEU EAC conformity declarations nor EU CE Notified Body certificates are accepted as substitutes. The certification body must be accredited by the national accreditation body of Azerbaijan. Certification scope, mandatory product lists, and applicable standards should be confirmed with AZSTAND prior to export, as Azerbaijan's mandatory certification list is subject to update.
target_standards: AZSTAND national conformity certification system (Azerbaijan Standardisation Institute)
GOST 12.4.191 (adopted) — Filtering half masks for protection against particles
GOST 12.4.028 (adopted) — Respirators — General technical conditions
AZS equivalents of EN 149 (where adopted by AZSTAND)
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese industrial respirators (GB 2626-2019, KN95) undergo China Compulsory Certification (CCC) administered by CNCA. The assessment involves type-testing by a CNAS-accredited laboratory and factory inspection by a CNCA-authorised certification body (e.g. CQC). A CCC certificate and the CCC mark on the product are the domestic market-access requirements. For medical-protective masks (GB 19083-2010), NMPA Class II medical device registration is required. Labour-protection (LA) certification is also applicable for occupational products. None of these Chinese certifications provide mutual recognition or exemption from Azerbaijan national conformity certification.

rows.gap: The entire conformity assessment must be re-run under the Azerbaijan national system. Key gaps: (1) Chinese CCC certificates and NMPA registrations do not satisfy Azerbaijan national certification requirements; (2) An AZSTAND-accredited or nationally recognised certification body must conduct the assessment; (3) Type-testing must be performed against the applicable AZS / GOST-adopted standard by an accredited Azerbaijani or recognised laboratory; (4) A valid national conformity certificate for Azerbaijan must be obtained before customs clearance; (5) The mandatory product list and applicable AZS standard numbers must be confirmed with AZSTAND, as these may differ from GOST or EN equivalents; (6) EAEU EAC marks are not valid in Azerbaijan — do not confuse EAEU neighbouring-country requirements with Azerbaijan national requirements.

rows.requirement: Labelling — Azerbaijani-Language Requirements for Respiratory PPE
rows.target_requirement: Products sold in Azerbaijan must carry labelling in the Azerbaijani language (Latin script, as Azerbaijan uses the Latin-based Azerbaijani alphabet). Required labelling elements for respiratory PPE typically include: product name and type designation; manufacturer name and address; applicable standard reference (AZS or GOST standard number); protection class / filtration grade (e.g. equivalent of FFP1/FFP2/FFP3 or KP1/KP2/KP3 under GOST); conformity certification number (from the national conformity certificate); instructions for use and storage conditions in Azerbaijani; expiry date or production date; country of origin. Chinese-only or Russian-only labelling is not sufficient for the Azerbaijan retail or B2B market — Azerbaijani-language labelling is required. Supplementary Russian labelling may be accepted in practice (GOST-legacy), but Azerbaijani is the mandatory national language. Confirm current labelling requirements with the importer or AZSTAND.
target_standards: AZSTAND labelling requirements for regulated goods sold in Azerbaijan

rows.china_equivalent: Chinese domestic labelling for GB 2626-2019 respiratory PPE must be in Simplified Chinese. Required elements include: product name; standard number (GB 2626-2019); protection class (KN90 or KN95); manufacturer name, address, and CCC certificate number; production date and shelf life; instructions for use in Chinese. Export packaging must be relabelled for Azerbaijan with Azerbaijani-language content — Chinese-language labels do not satisfy Azerbaijan market requirements.

Exporters must: (1) produce Azerbaijani-language labelling (Latin script) covering all mandatory elements; (2) reference the applicable AZS / GOST standard number (not GB 2626); (3) include the Azerbaijan national conformity certificate number; (4) include Azerbaijani instructions for use; (5) confirm with the local importer or AZSTAND whether Russian-language supplementary labelling is also required or acceptable in practice. Do not assume Russian labelling is sufficient — Azerbaijani is the national language and required for consumer-facing products.

rows.requirement: Conformity Marking — Azerbaijan National Mark vs. CE / EAC (Non-EAEU)
rows.target_requirement: Azerbaijan does NOT require CE marking (EU) or the EAC conformity mark (EAEU Eurasian Conformity mark). Azerbaijan is not a member of the EAEU, so the EAC mark is not a valid market-access mark for Azerbaijan. Azerbaijan's national conformity marking system is based on a national conformity certificate (sertifikat sootvetstviya) or declaration of conformity issued by an AZSTAND-recognised body. The physical mark or certificate reference appearing on the product or accompanying documentation reflects the national certification issued under the AZSTAND regime. There is no single, universally mandated pictographic conformity mark equivalent to CE or EAC for the Azerbaijan market — the conformity certificate number on the label and accompanying documentation is the primary evidence of conformity. Exporters should confirm with AZSTAND or the local importer whether a national conformity mark symbol is required on packaging for the specific product category.

The CCC mark is visible on the product and packaging. Medical-protective masks (GB 19083) carry the NMPA registration approval number on the label rather than a separate pictographic mark. Neither the CCC mark nor NMPA registration number grants any market access in Azerbaijan — they are China-only marks.

rows.requirement: Performance Requirements — Filtration Efficiency and Inward Leakage under AZS/GOST Standards
rows.target_requirement: Respiratory PPE sold in Azerbaijan must meet the performance requirements of the applicable AZS or GOST-adopted standard. For filtering half-masks (equivalent to FFP respirators), the primary standard is GOST 12.4.191 (adopted by Azerbaijan as the relevant AZS standard), which specifies: (1) particle filtration efficiency by class (KP1 / KP2 / KP3 — broadly analogous to EN 149 FFP1/FFP2/FFP3 class hierarchy); (2) total inward leakage limits; (3) breathing resistance (inhalation and exhalation resistance); (4) CO2 content of inhaled air limits; (5) mechanical strength requirements. Test methods under GOST 12.4.191 differ from both EN 149 and GB 2626 in specific procedures and thresholds — products must be tested against the applicable AZS/GOST standard by an accredited laboratory, not merely cross-referenced from Chinese or EU certificates. There is no horizontal RoHS-style chemical restriction on respiratory PPE under Azerbaijan national law.

rows.china_equivalent: Chinese industrial respirators (GB 2626-2019, KN90/KN95) are tested for: (1) filtration efficiency — KN90 requires ≥90% NaCl particle filtration; KN95 requires ≥95% NaCl particle filtration (using a 0.075 µm median diameter NaCl aerosol at 85 L/min flow); (2) total inward leakage; (3) inhalation and exhalation resistance; (4) dead space CO2 content. The GB 2626 test method uses NaCl aerosol, which differs from GOST 12.4.191 and EN 149 in both challenge agent specification and flow rate protocols. A KN95 result does not equate numerically to GOST KP2 or EN 149 FFP2 without re-testing under the target standard. No RoHS-equivalent chemical restriction exists in the Chinese GB 2626 PPE standard.

rows.gap: GB 2626 (KN95) test results cannot be directly substituted for GOST 12.4.191 test results without independent re-testing. Key gaps: (1) Challenge aerosol specifications differ (GB 2626 uses NaCl at 85 L/min; GOST 12.4.191 uses different test conditions); (2) Class designations differ — KN95 is not equivalent to GOST KP2 by definition; (3) Testing must be performed by an accredited laboratory recognised under the Azerbaijan national system (or a mutually recognised body, if any agreement exists); (4) No mutual recognition agreement between China and Azerbaijan eliminates the need for re-testing; (5) There is no horizontal RoHS-type restriction on materials — this is a genuine difference from the EU regime, and no additional chemical compliance step is needed for Azerbaijan under a RoHS-type framework.

rows.requirement: No RoHS / Hazardous Substance Restriction under Azerbaijan National PPE Regime
rows.target_requirement: Azerbaijan does not apply a horizontal RoHS-type hazardous substance restriction to respiratory PPE under its national regime. The EU's RoHS Directive (2011/65/EU, restricting lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs, PBDEs, and additional substances in electrical/electronic equipment) is an EU-specific measure and does not apply to the Azerbaijan market. Azerbaijan is not in the EAEU, so no EAEU-wide RoHS-equivalent technical regulation applies either. For respiratory PPE (passive filtering devices), which are non-electrical products, there is no standalone Azerbaijani national chemical restriction analogous to RoHS that applies to this product category. Exporters should confirm with local regulatory counsel whether any general product safety or chemical law imposes substance restrictions on PPE materials — but no such framework has been identified as of the dataset date.

rows.requirement: Regulatory Scope — Azerbaijan National PPE Regime (Non-EAEU, AZSTAND-based)
rows.target_requirement: Azerbaijan is NOT a member of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). The EAEU technical regulation TR CU 019/2011 (On the safety of personal protective equipment) does NOT apply to products placed on the Azerbaijan market. Azerbaijan operates its own national standards system under AZSTAND (Azerbaijan Standardisation Institute). Respiratory PPE standards are GOST-based or adopted equivalents (e.g. AZS analogues of GOST 12.4.191 for filtering half-masks, GOST 12.4.028, and/or adopted versions of EN 149). Conformity certification for regulated goods (including industrial PPE) is required under the national conformity certification system administered by AZSTAND and relevant competent authorities. Exporters must obtain a national conformity certificate (sertifikat sootvetstviya) or declaration valid for the Azerbaijan market — EAEU EAC marks and TR CU certificates are NOT accepted as equivalent in Azerbaijan.

rows.china_equivalent: China uses a mandatory CCC (China Compulsory Certification) regime for industrial respiratory PPE under GB 2626-2019 (KN90/KN95 non-powered particle respirators), administered by CNCA / SAMR. Medical-grade respiratory protection (GB 19083-2010) is regulated as a Class II medical device by NMPA. Labour-protection (LA) certification is also recognised for occupational safety products. Neither CCC nor NMPA registration is accepted as equivalent to Azerbaijan national conformity certification.

rows.gap: Azerbaijan sits outside both the EU single market and the EAEU customs union. Neither CE marking (EU) nor the EAC mark (EAEU) grants market access in Azerbaijan. The applicable route is national conformity certification through AZSTAND. Chinese exporters must: (1) identify which AZS or GOST-adopted standard applies to their specific respirator type; (2) engage an AZSTAND-recognised or nationally accredited certification body; (3) obtain a national conformity certificate valid for Azerbaijan; (4) ensure labelling in Azerbaijani (Latin script). CCC and NMPA certificates do not provide equivalence or mutual recognition.
